item.title: Different politics, common ground in crime
item.description:
Their political ideologies may differ, but when it comes to land grabbing, extortion, attacks, vandalism and looting, activists from rival parties appear to find common ground.
Several recent incidents have highlighted the trend, with police and intelligence agencies finding the involvement of some activists linked to the BNP, Jamaat-e-Islami and even the Awami League.
Police and intelligence officials said they had found evidence of political links among alleged masterminds, patrons and several suspects arrested over attacks on the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1 and content creator Salman Muqtadir’s studio. The two incidents have drawn significant attention in Dhaka in recent weeks.
Thirty-eight citizens have issued a statement condemning the incidents, while social and crime experts blamed the recent political transition, the use of muscle power under party banners and the deterioration of law and order.
They said the government could not evade responsibility and called for those involved, along with their patrons, to be brought to justice.
Meanwhile, Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has strongly condemned the armed attack and attempted murder of media workers at Rajshahi University.
The anti-graft watchdog called for the perpetrators to be brought to justice regardless of their political affiliations or influence.
In a statement issued on Monday, TIB also urged the ruling BNP and opposition Jamaat-e-Islami to take effective measures to prevent violent activities by their parties and affiliated organisations.
TIB Executive Director Dr Iftekharuzzaman said justice must be ensured for the journalists and students who came under attack.
“Attackers, their associates and patrons must be held accountable through impartial investigations, regardless of their political identity or influence,” he said.
BNP reserved-seat lawmaker Ferdousi Ahmed Misty and former BNP leader Md Hanif Mia have been accused of patronising and masterminding the attack on the Radda MCH-FP Centre.
Ferdousi Ahmed Misty resigned from Parliament following an instruction from BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman. Earlier, 14 BNP and affiliated organisation leaders and activists were expelled.
The party did not specifically mention the Radda attack in its expulsion notices, citing allegations of violating party discipline and engaging in unethical activities. However, several party sources said the measures were taken over the attack on the health centre.
Six BNP and affiliated organisation leaders and activists have been arrested over the attack.
Local political sources said those arrested include Saiful Islam Khokon, 48, a member of Shah Ali thana BNP, and Md Alam, 53, president of Ward 8 of Shah Ali thana Sramik Dal.
Nur Alam, the expelled president of Shah Ali thana Jubo Dal, was also arrested. He was expelled four years ago over allegations of violating party discipline and extortion.
Other arrested suspects include Rakib Ahmed, a former joint convener of Shah Ali thana Jubo Dal; Sarwar Alam, vice-president of Dhaka Metropolitan West Chhatra Dal; and Sazzad Hossain Mishu, a former member of the founding committee of Shah Ali thana Chhatra Dal.
Police said Sazzad also identifies himself as vice-president of the Dhaka district unit of the Jatiyatabadi Cyber Dal. Sarwar has also been expelled from the party.
Police have also found links to a former Chhatra League activist and Jamaat in the attack on Salman Muqtadir’s studio.
Police and the Detective Branch (DB) have arrested several people over the attack on the content creator’s studio and the New Guinea Properties bhaban.
Among those arrested is Mizanur Rahman, 59, son-in-law of the MP from Kushtia-2. He is named as an accused in the case.
Another suspect, Shah Alam Anik, is known as a former Chhatra League and Jubo League activist and a joint convener of the Muktijoddha Projonmo League.
At a recent monthly crime review meeting at Police Headquarters, Inspector General of Police Md Ali Hossain Fakir said there was no scope to consider an offender’s political or party identity.
“An offender’s only identity is that of a criminal,” he said.
DB chief Shafiqul Islam told Dhaka Tribune that many of those arrested over recent attacks and looting in the capital had political affiliations.
“They were arrested after their information was verified and preliminary evidence was found linking them to the incidents,” he said.
He said police had clear instructions not to consider political affiliations in criminal investigations.
“If anyone commits a crime and the investigation finds evidence against them, we do not consider their party identity. Whoever they are, they will be brought to justice if the allegations are proved. No one will be allowed to get away with crime,” he said.
BNP Chairman’s Adviser Advocate Syed Moazzem Hossain Alal said the prime minister and BNP chairman had repeatedly warned party leaders and activists against committing crimes under the party banner since the BNP returned to power.
“There will be no leniency if anyone commits a crime under the party banner,” he said.
Alal said taking action against party members accused of wrongdoing was not a new practice for the BNP.
“It has a long history. In the past, action was also taken against party leaders and ministers when allegations were raised against them,” he said.
Referring to the action against a reserved-seat lawmaker, Alal said she had made significant sacrifices for the BNP but was nevertheless instructed to resign and held accountable over the allegations against her.
Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar told Dhaka Tribune that offences could involve violations of social, legal, moral or party rules.
“Our constitution provides for action against those who commit offences, depending on their nature. No one will be spared if they commit a crime by using their party position or identity. Punishment is inevitable,” he said.
Thirty-eight citizens have issued a statement condemning the recent attacks, vandalism and looting.
They called for impartial, high-level investigations to identify those directly involved as well as the groups and patrons behind the incidents and bring them to justice.
In the statement, civil society representatives said political and muscle power were being used in different parts of the country to grab land, attack homes and occupy khas land in riverine areas.
Such incidents, they said, were creating fear and anxiety among the public and contributing to a worsening law and order situation.
Social and crime expert Dr Touhidul Haque, a teacher of University of Dhaka, told Dhaka Tribune that the recent political transition, the use of muscle power under party banners and the deterioration of law and order had contributed to such incidents.
“The government cannot evade responsibility in any way,” he said.
He said political activists from different parties had been found involved in the Radda MCH-FP Centre and Salman Muqtadir studio attacks, with several suspects already arrested.
“In most major organised crimes in the country, political leaders and top criminals work together,” he said.
He said the political landscape had changed, while the absence of some influential people from the country had created opportunities for others to attack properties, engage in gunfire, vandalism and looting, and attempt to seize assets.
“These incidents show that the rule of law is weak and law enforcement agencies are inactive, which is a matter of serious concern,” he said.
“Therefore, the solution must come from political leaders themselves.”

item.title: July warriors seek constitutional recognition, legal protection, rehabilitation
item.description:
Injured July warriors and representatives of families of martyrs of the July uprising on Tuesday called for constitutional recognition of the mass uprising, legal protection for July fighters and proper treatment and rehabilitation for those injured during the movement.
The demands were placed at the sixth meeting of the Special Committee on Constitutional Amendment, held at the Cabinet Room of the National Parliament Building with committee Chairman and Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed in the chair.
More than 60 representatives of families of martyrs and injured July warriors took part in the meeting and presented their views and proposals on various issues.
They proposed incorporating the July Declaration and the spirit of the July mass uprising into an appropriate part of the Constitution, granting immunity to July warriors, resolving legal complications they face, and expediting the trials of genocide and crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising.
The participants also proposed changes to important constitutional provisions, including the incorporation of a provision for a referendum on changes concerning the judiciary, Election Commission and caretaker government system to strengthen democratic institutions.
They stressed ensuring a safe and discrimination-free environment for women in politics, taking into consideration their participation in the July mass uprising.
During the discussion, a proposal was also made to permanently incorporate the spirit and declaration of the July mass uprising into an appropriate part of the Constitution.
The committee agreed to consider the proposals, said a press release issued by the Parliament Secretariat.
It also requested anyone having written proposals on constitutional amendments beyond those discussed at the meeting to send them to the committee for consideration.
Committee members Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman, State Minister for Planning Md Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki, State Minister for Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment Md Nurul Haque and Shakila Farzana attended the meeting.

item.title: Shoe garland hung on Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman sculpture in Jhenaidah
item.description:
A shoe garland was hung on a sculpture of Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman in the Central Bus Terminal area of Jhenaidah city, sparking anger among locals.
Photos of the incident spread on social media on Tuesday morning, reports Bangla Tribune.
The garland was removed later in the afternoon, said freedom fighter Kamaluzzaman, a former leader of the district Muktijoddha Sangsad.
Kamaluzzaman said the shoes were hung on the sculpture on Monday night.
“After learning about it, I went to the site with several freedom fighters and removed them. The sculpture was vandalized several months ago as well,” he said.
Jhenaidah Sadar police station Officer-in-Charge Md Asaduzzaman said police learned about the incident through social media.
“We are investigating the incident,” he said.
A meeting was held at the Jhenaidah deputy commissioner’s office on Tuesday evening.
Later, Deputy Commissioner Md Noman Hossain said police had been instructed to investigate the incident and take legal action.
Speaking on the matter, freedom fighter Siddikur Rahman said Hamidur Rahman was a source of pride for Jhenaidah and the entire country.
“He sacrificed his life during the Liberation War and became a symbol of heroism. The sculpture was vandalized before, and today’s (Monday's) incident is also deeply regrettable and condemnable. We demand a swift investigation and that those responsible be brought to justice,” he said.
Hamidur Rahman’s nephew Hafizur Rahman said the sculpture had been targeted repeatedly.
“I believe a group deliberately put the shoe garland on the sculpture. They do not want it to be installed in Jhenaidah. We demand a swift investigation and legal action against those responsible,” he said.
Abu Tawab Opu, general secretary of the Jhenaidah district committee of the Communist Party of Bangladesh, also condemned the incident and demanded an investigation and exemplary punishment for those responsible.
“The incident is an attack on the Liberation War, independence and sovereignty,” he said.
Deputy Commissioner Noman Hossain said the incident was “extremely regrettable.”
“We will identify who carried out this disgraceful act at night. We will discuss the matter with all sides and take action. I have asked the police superintendent to act swiftly,” he said.
The sculpture stands at the link point of the Jhenaidah-Jessore and Jhenaidah-Kushtia highways near the Central Bus Terminal, at the entrance to the city.
It was vandalized after the July uprising. Demolition work resumed on July 13 this year and continued until July 17. The district administration and other relevant authorities could not explain why the work was being carried out.
The district administration suspended the demolition work on July 18.
Recently, the district Muktijoddha Sangsad put up a banner at the site reading: “Repair work on the Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman Memorial is underway.”

item.title: Fuel price hike pushes Dacope boatmen toward alternative work
item.description:
Diesel price hike and declining passenger numbers have left boat operators in Dacope upazila of Khulna struggling to make ends meet, with many considering leaving the profession for alternative work.
Operating costs have nearly doubled following a Tk20-per-litre increase in diesel prices, while passengers are increasingly opting for road transport as road conditions have improved after the monsoon.
The 41km Kalabogi-Chalna route is served by 29 passenger boats. Each boat consumes around 8-9 litres of diesel per trip. The fare was previously Tk80 per passenger when diesel cost Tk115 a litre. Following the price hike, operators have raised fares by Tk10-12.
Boatmen said a boat usually carries 20-25 passengers per trip, making it increasingly difficult to cover fuel and labour costs. Only eight to nine boats are still operating regularly on the route, while most others have been taken out of service.
Boat owners must pay a driver Tk650 and an assistant Tk500 a day regardless of passenger numbers, further increasing their losses.
Sujit Mondal, Gaffar Hossain Gazi, Abdullah Gazi, Elahi Box, Khalek and Bidhan Sardar, who operate boats on the route, said passenger numbers were higher during the monsoon because many roads remain under construction or become muddy and difficult to use.
“Now that the roads have dried up, passengers prefer road transport to save time. At the current fare and fuel price, it is becoming difficult to keep the boats running,” they said.
Akbar Sardar, a trader travelling from Kalabogi to Chalna, said boat travel now costs more and takes longer. “During the monsoon, I used boats despite the higher cost because the roads were muddy. Now I use an engine-powered van to cut travel expenses,” he said.
Boatman Bakul Mallik said passenger numbers had fallen sharply. “We used to make a profit operating on this route. Now our income is barely enough to cover household expenses. If this continues, I will leave the boat and work as a day labourer,” he said.
Jafar Hawladar, who operates a boat for hire from Chalna Launch Ghat, said demand for reserved boats had also dropped. “No one has hired my boat in the past two days. After years in this profession, I am now considering switching to another occupation,” he said.
At Lakshmikhola ferry ghat, boatman Kamrul Islam said the fare had increased from Tk5 to Tk6-7 per passenger following the diesel price hike.
Nimai Saha, a diesel retailer at Chalna market, said a 200-litre barrel now costs Tk26,300, up from Tk22,300, while transportation from the Khulna depot costs another Tk200-250 per barrel.
Dacope Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Borhan Uddin Mithu said authorities were monitoring markets to prevent traders from charging excessive prices. “If there is a specific complaint against any diesel trader for overcharging, legal action will be taken immediately,” he said.

item.title: 30 banks suspend card, ATM, digital services until Oct 10
item.description:
Millions of bank clients across Bangladesh have been plunged into severe distress after key card, ATM, and digital transaction services were abruptly suspended across 30 commercial banks for system maintenance and network migration, with users complaining of zero to no prior warning.
The massive nationwide outage—which primarily impacts automated teller machines (ATMs), Point of Sale (POS) terminals, Cash Recycling Machines (CRMs), Quick Response (QR) payments, and online transfers—began at 9pm on Sunday and is set to drag on until 12pm on October 10.
The multi-day freeze stems from a scheduled system migration of the Q-Cash network, along with routine IT infrastructure upgrades across participating institutions.
Frustrated consumers flooded social media with complaints after encountering transaction failures during emergency medical payments, urgent purchases, and routine cash withdrawals. Many asserted that had banks properly alerted them in advance, they could have withdrawn cash or secured alternative payment options.
Responding to the public outcry, Bangladesh Bank Spokesperson and Executive Director Arief Hossain Khan described the simultaneous 30-bank blackout as a "coincidence," explaining that individual banks independently scheduled their annual maintenance routines within the same period after obtaining regulatory clearance.
"We have spoken with the respective banks to ensure whether they adequately informed and alerted their clients," Khan said, acknowledging the hardship faced by account holders.
The institutions affected by the service freeze include Bank Asia, Bangladesh Krishi Bank, Janata Bank, Bengal Commercial Bank, Community Bank, Jamuna Bank, Midland Bank, Meghna Bank, Mercantile Bank, Modhumoti Bank, National Bank, NRBC Bank, NCC Bank, Rupali Bank, Shahjalal Islami Bank, Shimanto Bank, Social Islami Bank, Trust Bank, and Uttara Bank, among others.
Although several banks claimed to have sent notices via SMS, social media, and official websites, consumers argued that the limited outreach failed to provide clear, actionable warnings for an outage lasting nearly a week.
Industry experts and central bank officials emphasized that while technical upgrades are essential for cybersecurity, future system migrations demand far more transparent and proactive communication to prevent widespread public disruption.
Customers have been advised to check the schedules of relevant services through their respective banks' SMS alerts, websites, mobile applications, or branch offices until operations return to normal.
For urgent transactions, customers may utilize alternative options, including other bank accounts, different cards, mobile financial services (MFS), or any authorized transaction methods.
However, risks of fraud increase during such periods. Customers are strictly urged not to share their card PINs, One-Time Passwords (OTPs), system passwords, or confidential banking details with any unfamiliar individual or entity.
Bank officials stated that if system migration or maintenance work finishes ahead of schedule, the affected services may resume earlier than anticipated.
While tech-based services across 30 banks are undergoing a temporary suspension, the country's overall banking system has not shut down. Nevertheless, the incident highlights the critical need for advance and transparent communication to minimize public inconvenience during planned system outages.

item.title: President seeks more Canadian investment
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Tuesday urged Canada to boost its investment in Bangladesh and expand cooperation in various sectors.
He made the call when Canadian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Ajit Singh paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban.
During the meeting, the Canadian envoy handed over a congratulatory message from Governor General of Canada Louise Arbour to the president.
In reply, Mirza Fakhrul thanked her for the message.
The president praised Canada's long tradition of democratic practices and sought its cooperation in institutionalizing democracy in Bangladesh.
He said the current government is facing challenges due to the prolonged absence of democratic practices and parliamentary traditions and has initiated necessary reforms to institutionalize democracy.
Ajit said bilateral trade between Bangladesh and Canada has exceeded 4 billion Canadian dollars annually, noting that there is further scope to expand trade between the two countries.
He also informed the president of the upcoming visit of a Canadian minister dealing with foreign affairs to Bangladesh.
The President called for greater Canadian cooperation in agriculture, food security, fertiliser, IT, outsourcing and other sectors.
He also sought increased Canadian cooperation in education, particularly in technical education, technology, nursing and medical fields.
On the Rohingya issue, High Commissioner Ajit highlighted Canada's support, saying the Canadian government has so far provided around 600 million Canadian dollars in assistance.
Mirza Fakhrul thanked the Canadian government for its continued support and urged Canada to play an effective role in mounting international pressure for the voluntary and safe return of the Rohingyas to Myanmar.
He further said more than 100,000 Bangladeshis are contributing to the development of Canada.
The president's secretaries and senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs were present at the meeting.
Political Counsellor of the Canadian High Commission Marcus Devies was also present.

item.title: ICT minister calls for global cooperation in AI governance
item.description:
ICT Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam on Tuesday has stressed the need for trust, capacity-building and international cooperation to ensure responsible and inclusive use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the public sector.
“The key question is not simply how quickly we adopt AI, but how wisely, responsibly and inclusively we govern and regulate it,” he said, according to a press release.
He made these remarks while addressing the inaugural session of an interregional conference titled “AI Governance in Practice: Practical Use Cases, Institutional Capacity, Innovation at Scale and Global Cooperation” in Istanbul.
The two-day conference, being jointly arranged by Korea, Türkiye, the Astana Civil Service Hub and UNDP, brings together ministers and senior officials from countries across the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Asia-Pacific region, along with representatives of UNDP and international development partners.
The minister said AI is no longer merely a technology of the future, as it is already transforming government decision-making, public services and development processes.
He identified trust, capacity-building and international cooperation as three fundamental principles for effective AI governance.
Referring to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s remarks at the UN General Assembly, he said AI should not create new forms of inequality but should instead help address existing disparities.
“Let us ensure that today’s digital divide does not become tomorrow’s AI divide,” he added.
He also called for greater technology transfer, skills development and affordable access to modern technologies to ensure that the benefits of AI are shared more broadly.
The minister expressed hope that the conference would create a platform for innovation, trust and inclusive technology where no country is left behind.
He reaffirmed Bangladesh’s strong commitment and support for the initiative.

item.title: Nagad to sponsor DRU Best Reporting Award 2026
item.description:
Nagad will sponsor the Dhaka Reporters Unity’s (DRU) ‘Best Reporting Award 2026’. This year, the award has been titled ‘Nagad-DRU Best Reporting Award 2026’.
Nagad and DRU jointly announced it at a press conference held at the Shafiqul Kabir Auditorium of the Dhaka Reporters Unity on Tuesday.
Awards will be presented for subject-specific reporting across a total of 26 categories, divided into two segments: print-online and television-radio.
Two of the categories for the best report will be open to all media outlets, with the awards presented on behalf of the president of Bangladesh.
A panel of 10 senior journalists from the country will select the best reports of the year after reviewing and evaluating the submissions.
DRU members can submit reports published or aired between October 1, 2025, and September 30, 2026, for nomination.
The deadline for submitting reports is October 14, 2026.
Speaking at the press conference, DRU President Abu Saleh Akon said recognizing reporters for the best reports of the year is a positive initiative that contributes to the advancement of journalism in the country. Since its inception, the Dhaka Reporters Unity has played this role, and the initiative has positively impacted journalism, he added.
DRU General Secretary Mynul Hasan Sohel said Nagad, the postal department's mobile financial service, is partnering with DRU for this year’s initiative. He said the homegrown service has quickly established a significant position in the country’s digital transaction sector.
“Nagad has partnered with DRU in three award programs, including this year’s event. We thank and welcome the homegrown service for its continued efforts to encourage journalism in the country,” he said.
Nagad Chief Commercial Officer Mohummed Shahin Sarwar Bhuiyan said, “Dhaka Reporters Unity is one of the leading organizations representing journalists who contribute to journalism in the country. We are delighted to be associated with such an initiative as a homegrown mobile financial service.”
“We believe journalists play an important role in highlighting various irregularities in society and serve as the eyes of the state on matters relating to rules and regulations. As always, we are partnering with this award to encourage better and more enriched journalism,” he added.
Nagad Chief Compliance Officer and Chief Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Officer (CAMLO) Muhammad Anisur Rahman Bhuyan, Nagad Head of Media and Communications Muhammad Zahidul Islam, Nagad-DRU Award Coordinator and DRU Organising Secretary MM Jasim, along with members of the DRU Executive Committee, DRU members and senior officials of Nagad, were present at the press conference.
Nagad first partnered with the DRU Best Reporting Award in 2021, when the award was presented at a grand ceremony.
It renewed its partnership in 2025 and is now joining the initiative for the third time in 2026, continuing its efforts to promote quality journalism in the country by recognizing some of the country’s leading journalists.

item.title: ONE Bank promotes Bangla QR among retailers in Uttara
item.description:
ONE Bank PLC organized a Bangla QR awareness program in Uttara Tuesday, in partnership with the shop owners of Zam Zam Tower, to encourage retailers to adopt digital payments and highlight the broader economic benefits of an interoperable digital payment ecosystem.
Muhit Rahman, managing director of ONE Bank PLC, highlighted the importance of Bangla QR in making digital payments more accessible and practical for small businesses.
He also conducted live Bangla QR transactions at participating retail outlets to demonstrate the ease of digital payments.
Speaking at the event, Rahman said: “For small businesses, the value of Bangla QR goes beyond payment convenience. Regular digital transactions can create a financial footprint and provide greater visibility into actual business cash flows. Over time, this can help bring small businesses further into the formal financial system and support their access to working capital and other banking services. This is an important economic opportunity as Bangladesh moves towards a more digitally enabled and less cash-dependent economy.”
The program also highlighted Bangladesh Bank’s measures to reduce the cost of Bangla QR payments, including the waiver of merchant charges and incentives for eligible transactions of up to Tk2,000 processed through the National Payment Switch Bangladesh (NPSB).
These initiatives aim to encourage wider acceptance among small retailers and promote everyday digital payments.
Customers can make Bangla QR payments through ONEApp and OK Wallet, offering a convenient way to pay participating merchants using their mobile devices.
The program forms part of ONE Bank’s efforts to support Bangladesh Bank’s vision of an inclusive, digitally enabled and increasingly cashless economy.
By expanding merchant acceptance and consumer adoption, ONE Bank aims to make digital payments a natural part of everyday commerce and contribute to a more connected financial ecosystem in Bangladesh.

item.title: World Bank: Subsidies failing Bangladesh’s poorest
item.description:
Millions of Bangladesh’s poorest citizens are being shut out of vital government support systems due to severe targeting inefficiencies, untargeted subsidies, and fragmented social safety net programs, according to a report released Tuesday by the World Bank.
The multilateral lender’s report, titled Bangladesh Development Update: Make Subsidies and Social Protection Work Better for the Poor, reveals a stark disconnect between state spending and poverty relief.
The World Bank notes that while the government allocates substantial fiscal resources—spending approximately 3.5% of GDP on energy, fertilizer, and social assistance—nearly half of the country’s poorest households receive no safety net support at all, leaving the most vulnerable exposed as national poverty rises toward 22.8%.
According to the global lender’s analysis, the fundamental crisis lies in structural leakages and regressive spending.
The report highlights that a disproportionate share of public subsidies continues to benefit higher-income households and well-connected commercial operations rather than the low-income families most impacted by persistent double-digit food inflation.
Generalized energy subsidies present the sharpest example of this misallocation, the World Bank finds.
The report stresses that blanket price reductions on electricity and imported fuels predominantly subsidize rich urban consumers and large commercial enterprises with high consumption volumes, rather than low-income households.
The World Bank also points out that systemic governance deficits and capacity payments to quick-rental power facilities absorb vast public funds, crowding out targeted cash grants for the rural and urban poor.
The World Bank further identifies deep-seated fragmentation in the safety net architecture itself. Its research demonstrates that over a hundred social assistance schemes operating across dozens of government ministries suffer from duplicate efforts, high administrative overhead, and outdated beneficiary registries.
The global lender reveals that non-poor households frequently capture social protection benefits due to subjective selection procedures and local patronage networks, while marginalized groups—particularly informal urban laborers and landless agricultural workers—remain excluded.
In the agriculture sector, the World Bank observes that bulk fertilizer subsidies intended to protect smallholder farmer livelihoods are frequently siphoned off by distribution intermediaries or commercial agricultural operations, undermining food security for marginalized rural families.
Similarly, the report notes that specialized food assistance programs, such as Open Market Sales (OMS) and food-for-work initiatives, suffer from supply leakages and geographic mismatch, failing to reach urban slums where hunger is most acute.
Inefficient subsidization
World Bank experts warn that maintaining this inefficient subsidy structure is fiscally unsustainable and socially regressive.
With tax revenues severely constrained at just 7.0% of GDP, the World Bank warns that the state can no longer afford to waste public funds on un-targeted assistance.
To fix these structural failures, the report calls for an immediate overhaul of Bangladesh’s social protection framework.
The World Bank recommends phasing out broad, price-distorting energy and agricultural subsidies in favor of direct, targeted cash transfers to verified poor households.
Its key priorities include consolidating fragmented food assistance schemes, fully integrating and expanding the government's Dynamic Social Registry, and transitioning to digital payment systems to eliminate ghost beneficiaries.
"Reforming targeting mechanisms and redirecting subsidies directly to those in need is not just a fiscal priority—it is a moral imperative," the report emphasizes.
The World Bank estimates that structural refinements to social safety nets alone could lift an additional 2.85 million Bangladeshis out of poverty.

item.title: Nur's GOP suspends Jasim Uddin’s membership, issues show-cause notice
item.description:
The Gono Odhikar Parishad (GOP) suspended the membership of Md A Jasim Uddin, who contested against NCP leader Hasnat Abdullah in the Comilla-4 (Debidwar) constituency in the 13th National Parliamentary Election.
The party also issued him a show-cause notice asking why permanent organisational action should not be taken against him for "breaching organizational discipline" and tarnishing the party’s image.
The party’s central office issued the notice on Tuesday. The suspension was ordered by its President Nurul Haque Nur and Acting General Secretary Hasan Al Mamun.
The notice, signed by GOP Office Secretary Syed Mahbubur Rahman, however, did not specify the allegations against Jasim Uddin.
It just accuses him of a “serious breach of organizational discipline” and tarnishing the party’s image, to which he has been asked to submit a written response within five working days to the central office.
The notice said permanent organizational action could be taken against Jasim Uddin if he fails to submit his response within the stipulated time or if his explanation is unsatisfactory.
Multiple attempts to contact Jasim Uddin by mobile phone for his side of the story went unanswered. He has made himself unreachable amid the media circus surrounding the case.
In the 13th National Parliamentary Election, Jasim Uddin contested the Comilla-4 (Debidwar) seat with the Truck symbol representing the Gono Odhikar Parishad.
He competed against NCP leader Hasnat Abdullah and secured 49,885 votes with the support of the BNP, who asked their own candidate to stand down in the constituency.

item.title: Coast Guard arrests three with firearms, ammunition in Cox’s Bazar
item.description:
The Coast Guard has detained three criminals with five locally made firearms and 17 rounds of live ammunition in Chakaria upazila of Cox’s Bazar.
Coast Guard media officer Lt Commander Sabbir Alam Sujon confirmed the matter on Tuesday.
Acting on a tip-off, a joint team from Coast Guard stations conducted a special operation around 1am on Tuesday in the Badar Awlia Ghat area under Chakaria police station.
The team detained three people and recovered four locally made single-barrel guns, one double-barrel gun and 17 rounds of live ammunition.
The detainees were identified as Akhtar Ahmed, 78, Md Tanvir, 21, and Rukomuddin, 42. All are residents of Cox’s Bazar.
According to the Coast Guard, a group of five to six people had been staying in the area to supply firearms to a gang involved in theft and robbery targeting commercial vessels at sea.

item.title: PM: Govt working to ensure investment-friendly environment
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday said his government is working to ensure a stable, competitive and investment-friendly environment for both domestic and foreign investors.
He made the remarks when a high-level delegation of Toyota Tsusho Corporation, led by its Vice Chairman Ichiro Kashitani, paid a courtesy call on him at his office at the Secretariat, said the PM's Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Shadhin.
During the meeting, the Toyota Tsusho delegation informed the prime minister about its plan to establish a Toyota automobile manufacturing plant in Bangladesh.
The delegation said the initiative would create employment, promote industrialization, facilitate technology transfer and help develop skilled human resources in the country.
They also discussed the expansion of Toyota's operations in Bangladesh, potential areas of investment and its long-term business plans.
Welcoming Toyota's interest in expanding its investment and operations in Bangladesh, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman said the government is committed to ensuring necessary policy support, infrastructure and other facilities for foreign investors.
He also highlighted the potential of waste-to-energy generation and renewable energy in Bangladesh, saying the government would extend necessary cooperation and support if Toyota Tsusho Corporation shows interest in investing in these sectors.
The Toyota side informed the prime minister that plans are underway to expand Toyota Bangladesh's distribution network to all divisional levels of the country to make its services and operations more accessible across different regions.
They also said Toyota Bangladesh would begin work in 2027 to establish a hybrid electric vehicle (HEV) manufacturing industry in an economic zone in Bangladesh under the vision of "With Bangladesh, For Bangladesh", with full-scale production expected to begin by 2029.
Toyota Bangladesh also expressed interest in contributing to human resource development in Bangladesh, particularly by creating technical and vocational training opportunities for young people, enhancing skills and developing a workforce equipped for future industries.
Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Prime Minister's Adviser on Finance and Planning Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir, Prime Minister's Adviser on Science and Technology Rehan Asif Asad and Prime Minister's Special Assistant for Overseas Employment in the Asia-Pacific region Dr Md Shakirul Islam Khan, among others, were present.
On the Toyota side, Toyota Tsusho Corporation Mobility Division CEO Shigeru Harada, Toyota Bangladesh Limited President Premmit Singh and other senior officials attended the meeting.

item.title: Trivedi meets Modi to boost Bangladesh-India ties
item.description:
Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi on Tuesday met Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, which is seen as further consultations amid efforts from both sides to take forward relations in a positive and constructive way.
Quoting diplomatic sources in New Delhi, BBC Bangla reported that his visit was intended to convey Dhaka's current stance regarding Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s potential visit to India.
However, there has been no official statement regarding this visit from the Indian High Commission in Bangladesh, India's Ministry of External Affairs, or Prime Minister Modi's office.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Monday said the visit of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to India will take place at a conducive time.
"I am hopeful about it. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has never said that he will not visit India. The Indian High Commissioner is making efforts, and hopefully, Delhi will be receptive to his views," Kobir said.
High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi, while talking to reporters in Dhaka recently, laid emphasis on proper preparations by both sides before the meeting between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi, noting that there is no benefit in rushing.
"We have to make sure that proper preparations are made because many issues will have to be discussed - trade, commerce, water - many issues. We are very positive about the future," he said in response to a question.
After a courtesy meeting with Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan on Wednesday, the High Commissioner said they have to give both Prime Ministers a convenient time.
"As far as the Prime Minister's visit is concerned, the atmosphere is absolutely positive," said the Indian envoy, noting that no discussion had been held about the timing or month, but the visit would definitely take place.
He said there would be no issues for which a solution could not be found if the two leaders met and sat together. "See, challenges will be there. If we think there are no challenges, that would be wrong."

item.title: Pakistan PM urges Imran Khan supporters to end protest march
item.description:
Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif urged the party of Imran Khan on Tuesday to call off a protest march moving through the country’s northwest towards Islamabad and re-enter negotiations with the government.
Supporters of the jailed former prime minister began the march on Sunday, demanding Khan’s release after several rounds of talks with authorities aimed at de-escalation stalled.
“I still ask them to come to their senses. End your long marches and sit-ins. Once you end them, we will certainly sit down with you and talk,” Sharif said, referring to the leadership of Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.
The Pakistani premier also warned of the demonstration’s negative impact on the economy, saying that undermining the government’s economic efforts “would amount to hostility toward the state.”
“We will not allow this to happen. The law will take its course. Protecting the lives and property of the people is our responsibility, and we will ensure this by all means,” Sharif said.
Authorities have been preparing for weeks for the possible arrival of demonstrators in Islamabad, with the march originally slated for September 27 and then postponed until Sunday.
An AFP journalist saw thousands of people take to the streets on Monday in support of Khan in Kohat district of Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which is ruled by PTI.
Khan, a hugely popular former cricket star, has been behind bars since August 2023 and faces scores of charges ranging from corruption to treason and inciting violence, following widespread anti-establishment riots in May of that year.
He and his legal team reject the allegations, branding them as politically motivated cases aimed at neutralizing his popularity.

item.title: Exploring the process of self-reflection and introspection
item.description:
Art embodies devotion, persistence, and sincerity.
Engaging in art transcends mere technical mastery; it represents a lasting commitment to honesty, patience, and profound personal expression.
An artist relishes the freedom of their thought process and employs the medium according to their feelings.
Dr. Abu Kalam Shamsuddin exemplifies these values as a painter. Additionally, he serves as a devoted professor in the Drawing and Painting Department at Khulna University.
Shamsuddin's current exhibition showcases artworks created from 2019 to the present year, 2026.
His pieces are executed in acrylic on canvas, as well as pen and charcoal on paper.
Photo: Ahadul Karim Khan/Dhaka Tribune
He produces numerous doodles, which are characterized as nonspecific, unfocused, or unconscious drawings made while his attention is diverted.
Doodles are simple illustrations that may convey concrete representational meaning or consist of mere shapes.
His drawings are notable for their experimental nature. Shamsuddin's innovative approach to art has garnered him a highly regarded reputation.
In addition to being an adept doodler, he is also a dedicated acrylic painter. Since the late 2010s, he has been an active participant in the Bangladeshi art scene.
He believes that doodling and drawing can enhance an individual's memory by utilizing just enough mental energy to prevent inattentiveness or carelessness.
A highly occupied professional, Shamsuddin engages in sketching either during lengthy phone calls or while attending extended meetings.
He even draws while conversing, doing so without any particular objective.
When Shamsuddin experiences distress or concern, and his creative imagination flourishes, the combination of pen and paper enables him to delve into his visions.
He documents his frustration, longing, joy, and various other experiences on paper, which serves as a reflection of his contemplative state.
His doodles reveal to the world his unique perspective and encapsulate the essence of what he has observed.
It is clear that the artist aims to evolve with a distinct style that could become a signature of his artistic creations.
Shamsuddin's acrylic paintings are regarded as predominantly realistic and semi-realistic, with a focus on self-realization, introspection, and self-observation.
Most of his artworks feature a single figure, which is himself, depicted in various movements.
His expression is typically realistic, showcasing himself in different configurations.
His pieces suggest the human form, often illustrating it in both conventional and unconventional manners.
The primary objective of his work is to emphasize the movements of the human body while also highlighting the inner struggles and torments experienced by the individual.
Photo: Ahadul Karim Khan/Dhaka Tribune
Occasionally, his artworks concentrate on figural movements and their significant articulations.
Shamsuddin is very meticulous about creating the ground of the canvas. To create the background for his paintings, the artist layers four to five times before making a level satisfactory enough for plunging deep into his subject easily.
Initially, Shamsuddin deliberately constructs the canvas's foundation using sharp, straight, twisted, and spherical lines, before shifting his focus to human figures.
At times, the artist experiments with crisscrossed lines, curves, circles, loops, as well as oval and square shapes—all of which converge to express his visions and thoughts.
These diverse forms also exhibit a spiral appearance. Many of his sketches include intricate details of human faces and emphasize significant aspects of a figure.
Certain forms and compositions add an aesthetic quality to his works. During the exhibition, lively forms and striking compositions offer a kaleidoscopic visualization for art enthusiasts.
Shamsuddin's paintings appear highly dynamic due to the incorporation of various shapes, expressive lines, and vibrant colors.
Shamsuddin focuses on subjects such as intimate relationships, personal perception, and the thought processes that analyze inner pain, struggle, and yearning.
Additionally, he pays attention to the socio-economic and political landscape of the country, which is deeply intertwined with his artistic expressions.
Thus, it is fair to assert that his paintings authentically mirror societal realities.
The backdrop of the majority of his works is filled with charming colors and gentle shades.
Throughout his career, Shamsuddin has concentrated on a very limited theme.
His artistic expression is characterized by figurative expressionism and surrealism; occasionally, he employs realism to depict light and forms.
The interplay of light and shadow is masterfully executed in his artwork, and he meticulously maintains a balance between the figures and the overall composition.
Photo: Ahadul Karim Khan/Dhaka Tribune
Achieving this equilibrium between these elements is quite challenging. Above all, his paintings are driven by technique and exhibit a significant degree of aesthetic appeal.
Shamsuddin is an artist who has keenly studied various facets of human existence.
The diverse elements of human life, including socio-economic structures and the lifestyles of ordinary people, significantly influence his artistic creations.
These components are carefully depicted in his pieces.
His ongoing quest for innovative themes has helped him establish a solid foundation in the representation of human life.
Shamsuddin is a figurative painter. He portrays the individual world and its mysterious phases through his personal notion, experience and thought process.
It can be easily said his paintings have been recorded through his inner feelings and deep observation of his living place, existence and nostalgia.
He uses soft strokes, which bring an animated hallmark to his works.
His strokes, lines, and sprinkled dots are all simultaneously natural and create a language which is alien to us.
Shamsuddin commenced his journey as a realist painter. However, over time, he has evolved significantly.
As a result, innovative compositions and various forms have been incorporated into his artwork.
He is a painter imbued with emotion, expressing what resonates deeply within him. A hallmark of his style is the recurring figure. The artist's objective is to convey emotions.
His figures lean towards the stylistic rather than the realistic.
Additionally, a notable aspect of Shamsuddin's work is his focus on the interplay between internal and external movement.
Takir Hossain is an art critic and cultural curator.

item.title: Vegetable prices fall in Dinajpur, farmers struggle to recover production costs
item.description:
Vegetable prices have fallen in Dinajpur markets as supplies of early winter produce increase, bringing relief to consumers but leaving farmers worried about recovering production costs.
Prices of some vegetables have dropped by up to Tk30 per kg compared with last week. The trend was observed at Bahadur Bazar and other kitchen markets in Dinajpur town.
Supplies of winter vegetables, including red amaranth, spinach, radish greens, cabbage, cauliflower, beans, radish, carrots, tomatoes, turnips, beetroot, and capsicum, have increased significantly.
Imported green chillies are selling for Tk90-100 per kg, while locally produced chillies cost Tk130-140, down Tk20-30 from last week.
Potatoes are selling for Tk16-30 per kg depending on variety, onions Tk40-45, eggplants Tk50-70, beans Tk150-160, carrots Tk140, tomatoes Tk120 and radishes Tk60.
A wax gourd costs Tk40 each, bananas Tk30 per four, while cauliflower and cabbage are selling for Tk150 and Tk60 respectively.
Vendors at Bahadur Bazar said early vegetable production had been bumper across the district, increasing wholesale supplies and pushing prices down. They said they were buying at lower prices and selling with small profit margins. They expect prices to fall further as winter sets in.
Consumers said the lower prices had reduced their household spending on vegetables. The fall in potato prices has also brought relief to consumers, although importers and traders are facing losses. Farmers, however, are concerned about the price decline.
Several growers in Ghughudanga of Sadar upazila and different areas of Phulbari upazila said favourable weather had resulted in good yields, but current market prices were making it difficult to recover production costs. They fear prices could fall further during the peak season, causing substantial losses.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension in Dinajpur, the district set a target of cultivating early winter vegetables on more than 7,150 hectares across 13 upazilas this season.
Favourable weather has led to cultivation on more land than targeted, while overall production has also exceeded expectations.

item.title: Murder accused flees court again, cop suspended
item.description:
A murder accused escaped from a Dhaka court for the second time on Tuesday, prompting authorities to suspend the police constable responsible for guarding him and form a three-member committee to investigate the incident.
Shariful fled from the court of Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Jamshed Alam on Tuesday. He had also escaped from court custody in 2025, making this his second escape from a Dhaka court.
A case has since been filed against him with Kotwali Police Station over the escape.
Mohiuddin Mahmud Sohel, deputy commissioner of the DMP Prosecution Division, confirmed the matter.
“Shariful, a remanded accused in a case filed with Kotwali Police Station, cleverly slipped out of his handcuffs and escaped from the court. He had been brought from jail as the case was scheduled for a hearing,” he said.
According to Sohel, Shariful took advantage of a moment when the police officer guarding him was distracted and escaped through another door. Police are working to arrest him, he added.
SI Md Morshed Alam, in-charge of the CMM court lock-up, filed the case against Shariful, while Constable Abdul Alim, who was responsible for guarding him, was temporarily suspended.
A three-member committee has also been formed to investigate the incident.
According to the DMP Prosecution Division, Shariful was brought to court on Tuesday for the scheduled hearing, but the proceedings could not take place as the witness failed to appear.
Later, Constable Abdul Alim was taking Shariful to the lock-up when the accused allegedly slipped out of his handcuffs and escaped through another door.
Shariful had previously escaped from court custody on June 19, 2025, while being produced before the Dhaka Third Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge’s Court in a case over the murder of teenager Jisan Hossain filed with Khilgaon Police Station.
After the hearing, Shariful allegedly assaulted a police officer while being taken from the courtroom to the lock-up, slipped out of his handcuffs and fled.
On the same day, Md Ripon Molla, then in charge of the court lock-up, filed a case against Shariful with Kotwali Police Station over the incident.
Shariful was brought from jail to court on Tuesday in connection with that case.
Shariful is the son of late Shafik Ahmed of Haripur village in Nawabganj upazila of Dinajpur.

item.title: Our failure to contain dengue
item.description:
The grim toll of Bangladesh’s ongoing dengue crisis continues to rise, exposing a chronic failure of public health management and municipal governance.
With the national death toll climbing past 280 as of October 6, daily hospitalizations nearing 2,000, and a sharp spike in infections hitting regional hubs like Chittagong, what should be a manageable seasonal illness has once again transformed into a deadly public health emergency.
That September registered as the deadliest month of the year proves that official interventions remain woefully inadequate, reactive, and out of step with reality.
The current surge also highlights a persistent breakdown in vector control and local administration oversight. Across Dhaka, Chittagong, and rural districts, residents routinely report invisible city corporation workers, irregular fogging drives, and unmonitored stagnant water at construction sites and public spaces.
While municipal authorities predictably shift blame onto public carelessness, the reality from finger pointing is more suffering and death - an outcome nobody wants in the country.
As such, we need an administrative apparatus that does not act only after hospital wards overflow. Spraying ineffective larvicides or launching sporadic "crash programs" after the peak transmission season takes hold is an exercise in public relations, not public health.
Simultaneously, we do need more public awareness and recognition that mosquitoes must be stopped from breeding.
Ultimately, as has been stated numerous times, dengue has long moved on from being an unexpected annual surprise. It is, and has been for some time now, an endemic threat that requires year-round, science-driven mitigation.
We need our health authorities across the country to abandon their seasonal complacency. Treating human lives as acceptable collateral in what has become an annual administrative failure is unacceptable. We must act with the urgency needed to halt this preventable devastation.

item.title: Lethal force is not the answer
item.description:
The latest incident of firing by the Indian Border Security Force (BSF), which left two Indian nationals critically injured, serves as another grim reminder of a persistent, unacceptable crisis along the Bangladesh-India frontier.
This recent shooting underscores a broader, fundamental reality: The routine resort to lethal force by Indian border guards is a systemic issue that threatens human lives and undermines regional stability, regardless of the victims' nationality.
That reports also suggest that the BSF personnel detained them and tried to push them into Bangladesh, and fired after they resisted, is also deeply concerning, and needs clarification and investigation into the matter.
For years, high-level diplomatic meetings and ministerial summits between Dhaka and New Delhi have concluded with repeated assurances that non-lethal weapons would be prioritized and border fatalities brought down to zero.
Yet, on the ground, it is safe to say that trigger-happy responses remain far too frequent for comfort.
Tragic incidents involving firearm usage along an international border, often over petty smuggling or unauthorized crossings, defy basic international law enforcement standards. Surely we can agree that lethal force must strictly be a measure of last resort against imminent threats to life.
This cycle of violence cannot be normalized and must be condemned by all. Border management between two neighbouring nations, that too with such deep economic and diplomatic ties, requires more restraint and operational discipline.
It is high time to move past platitudes and enforce strict accountability. BSF personnel who violate non-lethal mandates must face thorough, independent investigations and clear legal consequences.
Resorting to live ammunition against unarmed or fleeing individuals breeds public resentment, fuels cross-border tension, and ultimately undermines the spirit of bilateral cooperation. We expect better.

item.title: Three die of dengue in Khulna in 24 hours, 302 hospitalised
item.description:
The dengue outbreak continues to worsen in Khulna Division, with three more people dying of the mosquito-borne disease and 302 patients hospitalised in the last 24 hours until 8am on Tuesday.
Khulna Divisional Health Director Dr Sheikh Mosharraf Hossain disclosed the information on Tuesday afternoon.
According to the health department, two of the three deaths occurred at hospitals in Khulna district, while the other was reported at Khulna Medical College Hospital (KMCH). With the latest deaths, the dengue death toll in the division has reached 55 since January 1 this year.
Of the 302 newly hospitalised patients, 231 are receiving treatment at government hospitals and 71 at private facilities.
Khulna district recorded the highest number of new admissions at 143, followed by KMCH with 44, Bagerhat 35, Jessore 18, Narail 18, Satkhira 16, Magura 10, Meherpur eight, Kushtia seven and Chuadanga three.
Health department data show that 15,063 people have been infected with dengue in the division since the beginning of the year.
Of them, 13,379 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, while 1,263 patients are currently undergoing treatment at hospitals across the division.

item.title: LPG cylinders sell at Tk200-500 above govt-fixed price in Faridpur
item.description:
Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) cylinders are being sold at Tk200-500 above government-set prices in Faridpur, with consumers blaming inadequate market monitoring and alleged supply shortages.
The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has raised the price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), setting the price of a 12kg cylinder at Tk 1,837, up from Tk 1,585.
Consumers in Faridpur town, upazila headquarters, and remote markets said they are often forced to pay more than the fixed price despite LPG cylinders being available.
Depending on brand and size, cylinders are currently selling for Tk2,000-2,500 in different markets across the district, locals said. Prices are reportedly even higher in some remote markets in Nagarkanda, Saltha and Madhukhali.
Consumers said the rising cost of LPG is adding to the financial pressure on households already struggling with higher prices of essential commodities.
Two autorickshaw drivers, a hotel owner and a homemaker on Mujib Road in Faridpur town said authorities should strengthen market monitoring and ensure LPG is sold at the fixed price.
The price hike is also affecting small businesses, particularly hotels, restaurants, food shops and tea stalls that rely on LPG for cooking.
Several traders in Nagarkanda market said LPG costs more in village markets than at the upazila headquarters, increasing their operating expenses and reducing profits.
“Cooking costs are rising with the price of gas. Other essentials have also become more expensive. Overall, it has become difficult to run the business as before,” a hotel owner said.
Retailers, however, attributed the higher prices to supply shortages. They said they sometimes have to buy cylinders at higher prices and incur additional transportation costs, making it difficult to sell them at government-set rates.
“We are also buying gas at higher prices. When supply is irregular, we sometimes have to incur additional costs to collect cylinders. We do not want to charge customers more deliberately,” a retailer said.
Locals also alleged that regular monitoring by the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection was lacking despite widespread complaints of overpricing. They called for regular drives to ensure LPG is sold at government-set prices.
Faridpur Additional District Magistrate Susmita Saha said instructions had been issued to all upazila nirbahi officers and executive magistrates to monitor LPG prices.
